T>\nT kahan_sum(const std::vector<T>& data) {\n    T sum = 0.0;\n    T c = 0.0;\n    for (const auto& val : data) {\n        T y = val - c;\n        T t = sum + y;\n        c = (t - sum) - y;\n        sum = t;\n    }\n    return sum;\n}\n\n// Print results for floating-point arrays\ntemplate <typename T>\nvoid print_results(const std::vector<T>& data, const char* name = \"Result\") {\n    if (data.empty()) {\n        printf(\"=== RESULTS ===\\n\");\n        printf(\"Name: %s\\n\", name);\n        printf(\"Elements: 0\\n\");\n        printf(\"=== END RESULTS ===\\n\");\n        return;\n    }\n\n    const size_t N = data.size();\n    \n    // Compute statistics\n    T sum = kahan_sum(data);\n    T min_val = data[0];\n    T max_val = data[0];\n    for (const auto& val : data) {\n        min_val = std::min(min_val, val);\n        max_val = std::max(max_val, val);\n    }\n    \n    // Compute hash\n    hash h;\n    for (const auto& val : data) {\n        h.add(val);\n    }\n    \n    // Sample indices: 0, N/4, N/2, 3N/4, N-1\n    size_t indices[5] = {0, N/4, N/2, 3*N/4, N-1};\n    \n    printf(\"=== RESULTS ===\\n\");\n    printf(\"Name: %s\\n\", name);\n    printf(\"Elements: %zu\\n\", N);\n    printf(\"Sum: %.17e\\n\", static_cast<double>(sum));\n    printf(\"Min: %.17e\\n\", static_cast<double>(min_val));\n    printf(\"Max: %.17e\\n\", static_cast<double>(max_val));\n    for (int i = 0; i < 5; ++i) {\n        printf(\"Sample[%zu]: %.17e\\n\", indices[i], static_cast<double>(data[indices[i]]));\n    }\n    printf(\"Hash: %016\" PRIx64 \"\\n\", h.get());\n \"Result\") {\n    if (data.empty()) {\n        printf(\"=== RESULTS ===\\n\");\n        printf(\"Name: %s\\n\", name);\n        printf(\"Elements: 0\\n\");\n        printf(\"=== END RESULTS Each C element is still accumulated in ascending k\n// order, so the result matches the sequential reference.\nconstexpr size_t kThreadTile = 4;\nconstexpr size_t kBlockDim = 16;\nconstexpr size_t kTile = kBlockDim * kThreadTile;\nconstexpr size_t kBlockK = 16;\n\n// Generate pseudo-random values for matrix initialization\nconstexpr double getPseudoRndValue(const size_t N, const size_t i, const size_t j) noexcept {\n    return (((i + 1) * (i + j + 1) * 1299709) % (N * N)) / static_cast<double>(N * N);\n}\n\nvoid initMatrix(std::vector<double>& mat, const size_t N) {\n    for (size_t i = 0; i < N; ++i) {\n        for (size_t j = 0; j < N; ++j) {\n            mat[i * N + j] = getPseudoRndValue(N, i, j);\n        }\n    }\n}\n\n__global__ void matrixMultiplyKernel(const double* __restrict__ A, const double* __restrict__ B,\n                                     double* __restrict__ C, const size_t N) {\n    __shared__ double As[kTile][kBlockK];\n    __shared__ double Bs[kBlockK][kTile];\n\n    const size_t tx = threadIdx.x;\n    const size_t ty = threadIdx.y;\n    const size_t tid = ty * kBlockDim + tx;\n    const size_t rowBase = blockIdx.y * kTile;\n    const size_t colBase = blockIdx.x * kTile;\n\n    // Thread (tx, ty) owns rows ty + kBlockDim * i and columns tx + kBlockDim * j\n    // (interleaved so that a warp reads consecutive shared-memory doubles).\n    double acc[kThreadTile][kThreadTile] = {};\n\n    for (size_t kt = 0; kt < N; kt += kBlockK) {\n        for (size_t idx = tid; idx < kTile * kBlockK; idx += kBlockDim * kBlockDim) {\n            const size_t r = idx / kBlockK;\n            const size_t c = idx % kBlockK;\n            As[r][c] = (rowBase + r < N && kt + c < N) ? {"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-haiku-5-5","id":"msg_011CfywDdGHouotb7uNkE1ZE","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The matmul benchmark now runs its multiply on the GPU with a tiled CUDA kernel. The executable is still `matmul`, and only `matmul/matmul.cpp` and `matmul/CMakeLists.txt` changed. I built it with CMake out of tree in `/tmp`, so the repo has no build artifacts.\n\n**What changed**\n- **`matmul.cpp`:** `matrixMultiply` is now a CUDA kernel. It uses 64×64 output tiles per thread block, 4×4 outputs per thread, and 16-deep k-slabs staged in shared memory. Each `C` element still sums over `k` in ascending order, as the original did. Matrices are allocated on the device and uploaded before the timer starts. The timed region covers the kernel plus the copy of `C` back to host memory, so the result is in the same place as before. Initialization and validation stay on the host, and there is no CPU fallback. The output format is unchanged.\n- **`CMakeLists.txt`:** Enables the CUDA language, compiles `matmul.cpp` as CUDA, and sets `CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES native`. The minimum CMake version is now 3.24. The `-O3 -march=native -Wall -Wextra` flags are forwarded to the host compiler through `-Xcompiler`.\n- **Precision:** Kept as `double`, since the validation tolerance and the original output require it.\n\n**Results (RTX 3090)**\n- N=4096: about 435 GFLOPS (roughly 78% of the card's FP64 peak).\n- N=2048: about 344 GFLOPS on the first run, which includes launch overhead.\n- The original CPU build ran N=2048 at 0.17 GFLOPS (99 s).\n\n**Correctness**\n- `-v` validation passes for N = 1, 7, 17, 65, 333, 1000, and 1025, which covers sizes that aren't multiples of the tile.\n- The printed sums and samples match the original exactly. For N=512 the full `-r` hash also matches.\n- For some sizes, such as N=333, the `Hash:` line differs. Some elements differ by about 1 ulp (max relative 5.5e-16). The cause is fused multiply-add (FMA): `nvcc` contracts by default, and with contraction disabled on both sides the matrices are bit-identical.\n- I kept FMA because disabling it roughly halves GPU throughput (227 vs 435 GFLOPS at N=4096). If you need the `-r` hash to match the original's CPU output for every N, the switch is `-fmad=false` in the CMake flags. That costs the speed above.\n\n**Not done**\n- Multi-GPU is not implemented; the kernel runs on the current device.\n- `output.txt` is untouched."}],"container":null,"stop_reason":null,"stop_sequence":null,"stop_details":null,"usage":{"input_tokens":2,"cache_creation_input_tokens":578,"cache_read_input_tokens":50291,"cache_creation":{"ephemeral_5m_input_tokens":0,"ephemeral_1h_input_tokens":578},"output_tokens":2,"service_tier":"standard","inference_geo":"not_available"},"input_transformations":[],"diagnostics":null,"context_management":null},"parent_tool_use_id":null,"session_id":"95b4ac1b-f5dc-4d03-95e5-3f92417abfc1","uuid":"e0a10cc7-2d77-4e2a-8aea-213b5158a2e2","timestamp":"2026-10-13T08:39:49.287Z","request_id":"req_011CfywDcwgm79U2Zh2fpf4B"}

The `-O3 -march=native -Wall -Wextra` flags are forwarded to the host compiler through `-Xcompiler`.\n- **Precision:** Kept as `double`, since the validation tolerance and the original output require it.\n\n**Results (RTX 3090)**\n- N=4096: about 435 GFLOPS (roughly 78% of the card's FP64 peak).\n- N=2048: about 344 GFLOPS on the first run, which includes launch overhead.\n- The original CPU build ran N=2048 at 0.17 GFLOPS (99 s).\n\n**Correctness**\n- `-v` validation passes for N = 1, 7, 17, 65, 333, 1000, and 1025, which covers sizes that aren't multiples of the tile.\n- The printed sums and samples match the original exactly. For N=512 the full `-r` hash also matches.\n- For some sizes, such as N=333, the `Hash:` line differs. Some elements differ by about 1 ulp (max relative 5.5e-16). The cause is fused multiply-add (FMA): `nvcc` contracts by default, and with contraction disabled on both sides the matrices are bit-identical.\n- I kept FMA because disabling it roughly halves GPU throughput (227 vs 435 GFLOPS at N=4096). If you need the `-r` hash to match the original's CPU output for every N, the switch is `-fmad=false` in the CMake flags.
